prerequisites: To enroll in specific technology subjects (third year), students must have passed at least 60 ECTS credits from the basic training module subjects and the common subjects to the industrial branch module (first and second year).
Having passed the Applied Mechanics course.

Having taken the Elasticity and Strength of Materials course (third year, first semester), mastering concepts related to hyperstaticity, static equilibrium, stresses and strains, section forces (bending, shear, axial, and torsional), dimensioning and checking of sections, and establishment of force diagrams.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.

Know, understand, and apply the theoretical and technological concepts required to identify and propose structural systems, providing students with the necessary training to meet the performance requirements established in legislation and the required functionality.

Apply the strategies of scientific methodology: qualitatively and quantitatively analyze the problematic situation; propose hypotheses and solutions to solve structural problems of different complexity.
Adequately communicate knowledge, procedures, results, skills, and aspects related to structural design, using specific vocabulary and terminology, and appropriate means.

Work effectively in multidisciplinary and multilingual environments, integrating capabilities and knowledge to make decisions related to the design and management of structural projects in the industrial field.

Develop designs and projects in the field of industrial constructions according to the corresponding construction technology and making use of available techniques and tools for solving structural problems.
Know, understand, and apply legislation, specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards in the field of industrial constructions.

syllabus_topics: 1: Introduction to structural design. Concept of structure. Materials. Structural safety. Limit states. Static determination and indeterminacy of structures.
2: Pin-jointed structures. Statically determinate planar trusses. Classification. Determination of forces. Sizing of members. Instability.
3: Rigid-jointed structures. Analysis of rigid-jointed structures. Stiffness, distribution, and transmission of moments. Relationships between deformations and forces.
4: Actions on buildings. Applicable regulations CTE-SE-AE. Load hypotheses. Safety coefficients. Combinations.

5: Characterization of industrial buildings. Basic calculation schemes for industrial buildings. CTE-SE-A, CTE-SE-SE. Typologies of buildings. Trusses and lattice girders. Rigid-jointed frames. Sizing of structural elements. Roof materials. Purlins. Columns. Calculation of bracing elements. Wind girders.

6: Introduction to reinforced concrete. Regulations. Cement. Types of cement. Water. Aggregates. Admixtures. Reinforcement. Properties of fresh concrete. Properties of hardened concrete. Durability. Concrete designation. Adhesion. Arrangement of reinforcement.

7: Basis for reinforced concrete section calculation. Ultimate limit states. Serviceability limit states. Characteristic values and design values. Safety coefficients. Geometric and mechanical characteristics of sections.

8: Dimensioning of reinforced concrete sections. Simplified calculation diagrams. Exhaustion domains. Dimensioning of rectangular sections for simple and compound bending. Reinforced concrete columns. Simple compression. Minimum eccentricity. Buckling. Transverse reinforcement and shear force. Concrete contribution. Reinforcement dimensioning.

assessment_methods.method: Various tasks developed throughout the semester (practical tests, problems, deliverables, and partial assessments...)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a final grade of 5 or higher is required, along with achieving at least 40% of the maximum possible grade in each of the following partial components: the partial theory exam on reinforced concrete, the partial practical exam on reinforced concrete, and each of the other tests/deliverables (pin-jointed structures, rigid-jointed structures, industrial constructions). Students can renounce assessment by not attending the ordinary exam. In the extraordinary convocation, students who did not achieve at least 40% in tasks or the ordinary exam must take a final exam, where 100% of the final grade can be obtained, still requiring a final grade of 5 or higher and 40% in partial notes.
